newsitem.title: USA: Calif. regulators probe Pacific Genesis bond deals.
newsitem.headline: Calif. regulators probe Pacific Genesis bond deals.

text.p: The California Department of Corporations -- the state's securities regulator -- has launched a formal investigation of municipal bond deals underwritten by Pacific Genesis Group Inc, the department's top investigator said on Tuesday.

The investigation is focusing on the suitability of the bonds for investors, bond disclosure and Pacific Genesis Group's sales practices, Bill McDonald, the department's chief of enforcement, told Reuters. He said the investigation was the agency's first involving the municipal bond industry.
Pacific Genesis was not immediately available to comment.

Last September, state Treasurer Matt Fong called for the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission and the state's Attorney General to investigate several bond deals underwritten by San Francisco-based Pacific Genesis Group.
In these deals, Fong alleged that illegal payments of bond proceeds were made and that bond proceeds were used to retire private debts.
The bonds were issued under the state's so-called Marks-Roos Local Bond Pooling Act, which allows local governments and agencies to form joint powers authorities to finance capital projects.

McDonald said his department's investigation of Pacific Genesis was still in the "fact finding" stage. He said state investigators were currently reviewing about 28,000 pages of documents about the firm's bond deals.
"This is a very important case," McDonald said. "It's one of the most important cases we have now."
The California Department of Corporations regulates the sale of securities and licenses brokers and agents.
